The chart uses the notebook’s own schedule; the groups are counted on the model.
Weight decay shrinks parameters a little at every step, so they only grow when the data really asks for it — a habit that tends to help models generalise.
applies it only to weight matrices, and spares the biases and the normalisers’ gains.

text.tspan: × p, every step, apart from the gradient step
Older optimisers added the decay to the gradient, and
then rescaled it together with everything else, weakening it unpredictably.
) subtracts it directly — “decoupled” — so every decayed number shrinks by the same fraction at each step. That is why its effect can be computed exactly below.
